slots_and_copies.name: slot_0_chunk_chain
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Single sequential chunk chain at 0x0000: 11 chunks (12-byte header + payload) ending at 0x7edf; reader hypothesised to walk chain, verify each 4-byte magic and sum8 payload checksum, and reject/blank on mismatch. No backup copy, mirror, or generation counter found (each magic occurs exactly once). Bytes 0x7edf-0x7fff are unused 0xff tail.

io_driver_functions.notes: FALSE-POSITIVE seed: empty stub called on divide-by-zero by __divsi3/__modsi3 family; not save/checksum code (verified by reading save_related_functions.c and decompiled.c)
FALSE-POSITIVE seed: signed modulo (__modsi3-style). No SRAM/EEPROM/Flash MMIO, no callers in callgraph. Not a save writer/reader.
FALSE-POSITIVE seed: unsigned modulo (__umodsi3-style), sibling of 0x08050930/0x08050a00/0x08050898. Not save I/O.
Signed division (__divsi3-style) in same compiler-runtime cluster 0x0804fd1c-0x080514cc; textually called by 28 functions for arithmetic, not save I/O.

Generic memcpy (word+byte copy, dst=param_1, src=param_2, n=param_3). Plausible building block for SRAM flush/load but no call site in the 562 traced functions is proven to pass an SRAM (0x0e000000) address - literal pools are unresolved _DAT_ placeholders. CONFIRMED_STATIC as memcpy, UNKNOWN as save driver.
Generic memset (value param_2, count param_3). Same caveat as memcpy: no proven SRAM call site.
SWI 0x0b wrapper (CpuSet-style BIOS copy/fill). Used e.g. by FUN_08043f10 with dest masked to 0x05xxxxxx (VRAM). No proven SRAM use.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Main loop / boot dispatch (callgraph root with 13 callees); FUN_08000e24 is early init calling SWI copy and many subsystem inits. Save-load-at-boot would plausibly hang off this init path, but no chunk/magic/checksum code was found in its traced body.
caller_chains.how_mapped: callgraph.json edge 0x08036ec0->0x08000e24 plus decompiled.c body of FUN_08036ec0; bodies read in full. No SRAM literal (0x0e000000) appears anywhere in decompiled.c (0 hits).

caller_chains.trigger_context: Per-frame/per-entity update path (called 0x16 times in a loop from main loop, then FUN_0800d698(1),(2) = text/score rendering). Traced and excluded: renders text via FUN_0800cff8/FUN_0800d198, does not touch chunk format.
caller_chains.how_mapped: callgraph.json edges + full body reads of FUN_0802951c/FUN_0800d698/FUN_0800d43c/FUN_0800d198/FUN_0800cff8.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Name/text rendering: memcpy of 0x19-byte string templates to stack, then tile writes. Traced and excluded as save caller (representative of all 4 textual memcpy callers).

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip one byte inside BATT payload (currently all-zero) without checksum repair (stored checksum at 0x1a is over payload only and payload is zero, so also try LINE)

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip one byte in LINE payload data region (e.g. file 0x5658, payload+0x45c) without repairing LINE checksum at 0x51fa
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If sum8 is enforced on load, whole save (or LINE chunk) is rejected and game reverts to blank/default, matching PACKET cold-reload probe behaviour. Repair: set u16 at 0x51fa to sum(LINE payload bytes)&0xffff.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Corrupt LINE checksum stored at 0x51fa (payload+header+10) by +1, payload unchanged
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Checksum mismatch on load; predicted rejection/blanking of save. Distinguishes checksum enforcement from magic-only validation.

fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Payload length and next-chunk offset shift by 1; SEAS magic no longer at expected offset. Predicted chain desync/rejection. Tests whether reader trusts header sizes or uses fixed table.

open_questions: Identity/address of the true chunk serializer/deserializer and SRAM (0x0e000000) byte-copy driver: not found in the 562 trace-guided functions; decompiled.c contains zero literals for 0x0e000000, 0x040000d4 (DMA3), 0x04000204 (WAITCNT), and none of the chunk magics or payload sizes (12400, 8256, 0x2040, 0x1f4, 0xabc) as immediates, because literal pools surface as unresolved _DAT_ placeholders and most calls are UNRECOVERED_JUMPTABLE indirect jumps absent from callgraph.json.
RAM mirror addresses (0x02xxxxxx/0x03xxxxxx) for every chunk payload: unresolved for the same reason; no field can be honestly assigned a RAM address from workspace files alone.
Meaning of header u16 at +4 (1 for blob chunks incl. STAT, 0 for 16-byte record arrays): version, flags, or is-array discriminator?

Why WSLU payload == LINE[0:500] and SEAS payload == LINE[0:2748] byte-for-byte: aliased/overlapping RAM source pointers in the descriptor table, or three buffers initialised from one ROM default template?

Origin of 'Debug Message LOST' (preceded by 0x0e) at payload+0x103/+0x104 in WSLU/LINE/SEAS, and of stale-looking engine-table data (charset '0123456789ABCDEFL', 'IDCT'/'UpSample'/'Blit' strings, scale tables) inside LINE payload beyond +0x45c: leftover workspace in a large save struct, or deliberate embedded data?

Nature of varying tail byte at 0x7ffc (0x08/0x80/0xb0) in the unused 0xff tail: uninitialised SRAM garbage, tick counter, or a global integrity byte as PACKET's mutation probe suggests? It is provably not a deterministic checksum of the rest of the file (rest is byte-identical while it changes).

Internal semantics of BATT/PITC 16-byte records (775/400 entries, all zero in these fresh/beta samples), LINE small-int array from payload+0x45c, and OPTS bytes 01 01 00 00 ff 00 ff 00: need a mutated/gameplay-progressed save or paired save-state RAM dump to map.

Whether the reader enforces sum8 on every chunk, only on some, or falls back per-chunk vs whole-save blanking on mismatch (PACKET probe: integrity_check_confirmed, reverted_to_blank_on_mutation at 0x7ffc - offset is outside the chunk chain, so probe interpretation is unresolved).
